title: New Feathered Dinosaur is the First Megaraptor Discovered in Europe - Nautilus
gist: A new Cretaceous feathered megaraptor was identified from a partial braincase found on the Isle of Wight in 1924 and left in a Natural History Museum drawer for a century. It is the first megaraptor found in Europe and informs megaraptor migration.

insights.claim: A new feathered dinosaur species from the Isle of Wight is the first megaraptor discovered in Europe, adding a piece to the puzzle of megaraptor migration.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Low direct market relevance; a general-interest science signal on how fossil finds revise dinosaur biogeography.

insights.claim: The species was identified from a partial braincase collected in 1924 by an amateur paleontologist that sat in a drawer at England's Natural History Museum for about a century.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Archived collections can hold undiscovered value; re-examination with new tools yields discoveries.
insights.locator: A team of paleontologists identified the new species

insights.claim: Researchers used micro-CT scans to build 3D models of the interior and exterior of the century-old skull, enabling the identification.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Non-destructive imaging unlocks legacy collections; a general pattern across science.
